meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on Owen's zero, Hale, and did anyone hear from him first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me why there's a zero at all.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing that down. Students draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Pull it up, then. And who else has seen it?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Seventeen-year-olds misremember Shakespeare all the time, and that costs marks, not the whole essay. You skipped my question, Hale: who else has seen this?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final essay, that's what an outline is for. Hand me both.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Being stuck is what it means, and he said it put on the spot by the teacher who'd already decided. So where is this going?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in class against an essay he had weeks for, of course it's cleaner. You've shown me a pile, now tell me what you're actually proposing.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Not leaning on it, and yet it made it into the room. Its maker's own guide is in my bag, and it says that number can't carry a punishment by itself.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4: private, not in front of his class, finished before December 1, and in writing tonight, with copies of everything you've shown me, that nothing goes on his file. He'll sit it to put this behind him, not because he did anything.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
It works when it's in my inbox tonight, with the December 1 date and copies of everything you showed me.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday the 12th, after school, and the time goes in tonight's email. Ten minutes.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Plus Thursday the 12th after school, and copies of everything you showed me. Then yes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The email. Tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the 12th, not in front of his class, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require that agreement in writing, with the December 1 date and copies of every document you showed me. I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school Thursday the 12th, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants all of it in writing tonight, with copies of your documents and the rewrite marked before December 1; that is the fair outcome, procedure 4.4, reached before her call.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, checkable and tied to Owen's own file, so her defence had nowhere to go.
What cost ground: Twice leaving her question about who else had seen the evidence unanswered, because each dodge kept her on the attack and made the deal slower to reach.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's writing between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked who else had seen the evidence, answer it in one plain sentence before moving to your next document.
